verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Two rewritings. (i) Coordinates: the Lean writes the cylindrical divergence in the regular similarity coordinate s = r²/2, as √(2s)·∂_s S + k·S/√(2s); since r = √(2s) and ∂_r = r·∂_s this is exactly (∂_r + k/r)S, and `radialDivergence_eq_deriv` (LeadingStress.lean:291) records that identification by stating the same quantity as deriv in r plus k·S/r. The paper's two cases k=2 (angular) and k=1 (axial) appear as `radialDivergence 2` and `radialDivergence 1`. (ii) The residual: the paper's R_θ^{(0)}, R_z^{(0)} are the θ- and z-components of the leading residual with radial viscosity retained and axial viscosity omitted; Lean states the identity for the full Cartesian Navier–Stokes residual component plus the exact axial-viscosity term (`thetaAxialViscosity`, `axialAxialViscosity`) on the left, which is the same quantity. Lean asserts the relation for the concrete constructed pair `physicalStressTheta`/`physicalStressAxial` (the q^{-A-1/2}-pullbacks of `theta`/`axial`) rather than positing a solvability condition on an unspecified T, i.e. the paper's "We construct physical stress components ... satisfying" is discharged. The statement carries side hypotheses 0 < h < 1/2, t < 1, positive radial energy and P.f ≠ 0 at the point; the paper's display is unconditional at this point in the outline.
